facts.fact: ARPCE's digital postal addressing project, run with town halls and partner administrations, was launched in April 2022, has had a legal framework since July 2025 in the decree on national postal codification, and was presented in Brazzaville on 15 October 2026.

COG.note: The document states no authentication service.
A speaker only proposes linking town halls and hospitals for birth acts and a unique ID number; no link is stated as planned or in service.
The document says nothing on e-procurement.
The document says nothing on the central bank's payments role.
No digital civil register is stated; birth acts are only a proposed outcome of town hall and hospital interconnection.
The document says nothing on consumer protection in digital finance.
The document says nothing on cross-border payments.
A data exchange platform is named only as something addressing should interoperate with; its state is not stated.
The document states no identity law or bill.
Sovereignty is mentioned only in general terms and as a Livre Blanc orientation; no plan or rule on state data is stated.
The document says nothing on government payments to people.
No ID enrolment count or share is given.
A unique identification number is only advocated by a speaker; no number at birth is provided for or in service.
The document says nothing on who runs the ID system.
A unique number linked to the universal health insurance fund is only advocated; no register keyed on the ID number is stated.
The document states no national ID system; digital identity is named only as something addressing should interoperate with.
Town halls are named as addressing partners and entry points, with no word on their connection.

systems.country_label: 94.1% mobile telephony penetration, per ARPCE's director general, 2026-10-15

COG.note: The 94.1% is a telephony penetration rate, not a share of people owning a phone.
The e-money account shares (under one woman in three, over four in ten people) are not a named survey of adults with a bank or mobile money account.
No civil registration office entering events digitally is stated.
Electronic money accounts are mentioned only as an inclusion share; no service or interoperability is stated.
The document says nothing on electronic payment of taxes or fees.
